clue.text: Funny ship from an opera's central part

definitions.text: Funny ship from an opera's central part

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so these letters come out in a strange new order
central part signals the middle letter of the word opera's

explanation.surface: A comic vessel lifted from the heart of an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny' shuffles SHIP FROM AN plus E, the middle letter picked by 'central part' from opera, and the whole clue describes Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera takes its title from a fictional Royal Navy vessel, so the funny ship belongs to that work.

clue.text: Transport system provided by some trolleybuses

indicators.note: provided by means supplied from within the words that follow, so the letters lie inside them

explanation.surface: A city's transit network is supplied by a fleet of trolleybuses.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground railway serving a city, such as the Paris network, is called by this name.

clue.text: Pilot's first craft about to take off and bank

indicators.note: first signals that only the opening letter of the word Pilot's is used
about means surrounding, so one piece sits round the other here

parts.note: craft means art or skill
to take off someone is to mimic them, to ape them

explanation.surface: A pilot's first plane takes off and banks into a turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' looks like flying and 'bank' like a turning aircraft, but take off means mimic and bank is the definition: a raised wall or embankment.
explanation.definitionFit: A parapet is a low protective wall or earthen rampart, a kind of raised bank.

clue.text: One song in performance with less feeling

definitions.meaning: an item in a show or a set, such as a song
comparative of numb: more deadened in sensation

explanation.surface: A singer delivers a song mechanically, without much emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is the comparative of numb, pronounced differently from the counting word.
explanation.definitionFit: A song in a show is called a number, and something more deadened in sensation is numb-er.

clue.text: Who's employed with respect to trees at work

definitions.text: Who's employed with respect to trees at work

parts.note: for can mean as regards, as in 'for my part'

indicators.note: at work means busy or in action, signalling that the letters of trees get rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about who is employed in looking after trees.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a person employed to look after trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodland worker employed to manage and look after trees in a forest.

clue.text: Make pounds in easier dealing

indicators.note: in places the pounds inside the rearranged letters
dealing as in dealing cards: the letters of easier are shuffled out

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling (libra)

explanation.surface: Making money through easier trading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dealing' rearranges EASIER into REAISE, and 'in' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a sum of money from a sale is to realise it, as in realising a profit.

clue.text: Job beset by drink writing at length religious statement

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the job sits inside the drink

parts.note: ales are drinks of beer
a post is a job or position
a screed is a long piece of writing

explanation.surface: Someone holding a job is plagued by drink while writing at great length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' looks like the biblical figure, fitting the religious theme, but it is just a post.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apostles' Creed is an early Christian statement of faith recited in church services.

clue.text: Teacher: I put emphasis on marks first of all

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means sitting above, so the marks letter comes before the rest
first of all signals the opening letter of the word marks

parts.note: stress is emphasis

explanation.surface: A teacher insists that she puts emphasis on marks above all else.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'put on' means placed after, so I and STRESS follow the M.
explanation.definitionFit: Schoolmistress is the old word for a female teacher, often shortened.

clue.text: Home Counties Tory in fear of Parliamentary procedure

parts.note: the Home Counties around London are in the south-east of England, SE
CON is short for Conservative, the Tory party
dreading means being in fear of

explanation.surface: A Tory in the Home Counties fears a parliamentary process.
explanation.walkthrough: The Home Counties are the counties surrounding London, in England's south-east.
explanation.definitionFit: A bill's second reading is the stage in Parliament where its general principles are debated.

clue.text: Tory leader captivated by Lord Mandelson perhaps

indicators.note: captivated by means held inside, so one piece is enclosed

parts.note: a lord is a peer of the realm

indicators.note: leader signals the first letter of the word Tory

explanation.surface: A Conservative leader charmed by Lord Mandelson, the Labour grandee.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter Mandelson is a Labour politician later made a life peer; 'Lord' gives PEER while 'Mandelson perhaps' is a first-name example.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandelson's first name is an example of a man's given name, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Fish in the sea's spread

indicators.note: in places the fish inside the word for the sea's

parts.note: marine means of the sea
a gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: Fish swimming in the vast spread of the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' looks like the sea's expanse but means something put on bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Margarine is a butter substitute that people spread on bread.

clue.text: Sunday Telegraph initially to keep control of latest news

indicators.note: initially signals the opening letter of the word Telegraph

parts.note: to oppress is to keep people under harsh control

explanation.surface: A Sunday paper struggles to keep control of breaking news.
explanation.definitionFit: Late items squeezed into a newspaper after printing began were headed with this label for breaking news.

clue.text: Enjoying taking in right song's first part

indicators.note: taking in means enclosing, so the right goes inside

parts.note: being into something means enjoying it

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys singing the right opening of a song.
explanation.definitionFit: An introduction or opening passage of a piece of music is often shortened to this informal word.

clue.text: See Elizabeth's player put in place

parts.note: lo is an old exclamation meaning look or see
Cate Blanchett played Queen Elizabeth I in the 1998 film Elizabeth

explanation.surface: Look at the actor who played Elizabeth being cast in the role.
explanation.definitionFit: To position or situate something is to set it in a particular spot.

clue.text: Fruitcake containing two drugs

parts.note: crack is a form of cocaine
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A fruitcake laced with two different drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two drugs' gives two pieces; 'containing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruitcake is slang for an eccentric or mad person, as is crackpot.

clue.text: Man of the cloth to tear around always

indicators.note: around means the tearing word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to rend is to tear
ever means always

explanation.surface: A clergyman inclined always to be tearing around.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleric, someone wearing clerical dress, is addressed with this title.

clue.text: Radioactive element favoured in naval battle

indicators.note: in places favoured inside the battle's name

parts.note: Actium, 31 BC, where Octavian defeated Antony and Cleopatra at sea
in can mean in fashion or favoured

explanation.surface: A radioactive substance gaining favour during a sea fight.
explanation.definitionFit: Actinium is a radioactive metallic chemical element, atomic number 89.

clue.text: Gangster stole one

parts.note: a stole is a scarf-like wrap
an ace counts as one

explanation.surface: A gangster has stolen something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stole' looks like a verb about crime but is the noun for a wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Capone's nickname, and the title of gangster films; a famous mobster.

clue.text: Vessel taking catch around deck

indicators.note: around means the catch goes round the vessel

parts.note: to fish is to catch, or a fish is a catch
an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: A ship takes its catch round the deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' and 'deck' suggest ships, but the vessel is an urn and deck is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck a room is to adorn or fit it out, as when you equip it with furniture.

clue.text: Virgin Atlantic finally gets urgency

indicators.note: finally signals the last letter of the word Atlantic

parts.note: haste is urgency

explanation.surface: Virgin Atlantic airline finally gets moving with urgency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virgin Atlantic' reads as the airline, but Virgin is the definition, an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Pure and sexually inexperienced; chaste is used of virginal people.

clue.text: Plants ecstasy under woman's accessory

indicators.note: under in a down clue means placed below, after the other pieces

parts.note: her is the possessive meaning a woman's
a bag is a fashion accessory
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Drugs found tucked under a woman's handbag among plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Herbage is a collective word for herbaceous vegetation such as grass.

clue.text: Charmer giving pretence of being a knight

parts.note: a sham is a pretence
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A charmer only pretends to be a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charmer' suggests a smooth talker; here it is someone who works charms or spells.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribal healer and priest who works magic and spells, so a literal caster of charms.

clue.text: Old hooligan not caught in old football ground

indicators.note: not signals that the caught letter is dropped

parts.note: rockers were leather-clad 1960s British youth gang members who fought mods
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A veteran hooligan evades arrest at a former football stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: Roker Park was Sunderland AFC's ground until 1997; rockers were 1960s British motorbike gangs.
explanation.definitionFit: Roker Park was the long-time home stadium of Sunderland football club, now demolished.

clue.text: One Nottingham Forest playmaker of old

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
Sherwood Forest lies in Nottinghamshire

explanation.surface: A Nottingham Forest midfield playmaker from years past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nottingham Forest' and 'playmaker' suggest the football club, but it is Sherwood Forest and a maker of plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Isherwood co-wrote plays with W. H. Auden in the 1930s, a dramatist of an earlier era.

clue.text: Veteran serviceman extremely deprived

indicators.note: deprived at the extremes: both end letters are taken away

parts.note: a soldier is a serviceman

explanation.surface: An old soldier living in extreme poverty.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldie is an informal term for an old person or a longstanding thing, a veteran.

clue.text: Isometric exercises being sexy

indicators.note: exercises means works over, putting the letters through movements into a new order

explanation.surface: Isometric gym exercises being sexy.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun for the quality of arousing sexual desire, the state of being erotic.

clue.text: Poet from university tucking into port

indicators.note: tucking into means going inside the port

parts.note: Aden is a port in Yemen

explanation.surface: A poet from a university tucks into port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' suggests the drink but is the Yemeni harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: W. H. Auden was an Anglo-American twentieth-century poet.

clue.text: Revolutionary guard gets further education in gambling game

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Marxist revolutionary

indicators.note: gets here means takes in, so the guard holds the education inside

parts.note: a minder is a bodyguard
FE is the British abbreviation for further education

explanation.surface: A revolutionary's bodyguard goes to college to study gambling.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemin de fer is a casino card game, a variant of baccarat.
